message.content:
**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference Guide to Its Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium, 99.98 %), H‑2 (deuterium, 0.02 %), H‑3 (tritium, trace) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈1/11 of air) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (120.95 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat capacity (gas) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusivity | Extremely high (≈0.1 cm² s⁻¹ at STP) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0008 M) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Diatomic molecule | H₂ (most stable form) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Highly flammable; explosive mixture with air (4–75 % H₂) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Reactivity with halogens | Forms hydrogen halides (HF, HCl, HBr, HI) |
| | Acidic behavior | HF is a weak acid; HCl, HBr, HI are strong acids |
| | Hydride formation | Forms metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | H₂O, HF, NH₃ exhibit hydrogen bonds; H₂ itself does not |
| | Role in stars | Fusion of H to He powers stars; proton–proton chain, CNO cycle |
| | Isotopic chemistry | Deuterium forms D₂O (“heavy water”); tritium is radioactive (β⁻ decay) |
| **Spectroscopic Features** | Rotational spectrum | Microwave region (≈2.1 cm⁻¹) |
| | Vibrational spectrum | Infrared (≈4400 cm⁻¹) |
| | Electronic transitions | UV (≈121.6 nm Lyman‑α line) |
| **Applications & Uses** | Fuel cell technology | Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFC) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) + liquid oxygen (LOX) |
| | Chemical industry | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, etc. |
| | Medical imaging | Deuterium labeling in NMR/MRI studies |
| | Nuclear fusion research | Deuterium–tritium fusion experiments |
| **Safety & Handling** | Explosion limits | Lower: 4 %, Upper: 75 % (air) |
| | Health hazards | Inhalation of high concentrations can cause hypoxia; HF is corrosive |
| | Storage | Requires cryogenic tanks (LH₂) or high‑pressure cylinders (compressed gas) |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe.
- **Diatomic gas**: Exists as H₂ under normal conditions; highly reactive and flammable.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive).
- **Key role in energy**: Fuels stars via nuclear fusion; used in rocket propulsion and fuel cells.
- **Chemical versatility**: Forms a wide range of compounds—from simple hydrides to complex organic molecules—and participates in both covalent and ionic bonding.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
